sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: All countries have national myths.
sentences.zh: 所有国家都有自己的民族神话。

sentences.en: Here in the United States, Thanksgiving evokes the warm glow of intercultural contact.
sentences.zh: 在美国，感恩节唤起了跨文化接触的温馨氛围。

sentences.en: European settlers were struggling to make it in the New World,
sentences.zh: 欧洲定居者曾在新世界艰难求生，

sentences.en: and Native American tribes were eager to help.
sentences.zh: 而美洲原住民部落则热切地施以援手。

sentences.en: If we were to think a little more deeply and a little more critically,
sentences.zh: 如果我们进行更深一层、更具批判性的思考，

sentences.en: we might remember other stories from history classes.
sentences.zh: 我们或许会想起历史课上的其他故事。

sentences.en: These are tales of exclusion and expulsion,
sentences.zh: 这些是关于排挤与驱逐的故事，

sentences.en: of Native American tribes pushed out from their homelands
sentences.zh: 讲述了美洲原住民部落被赶出世代家园的故事，

sentences.en: as settlers colonized the continent.
sentences.zh: 随着定居者对这片大陆的殖民。

sentences.en: But there's a third story you might not have heard.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个你可能未曾听闻的第三个故事。

sentences.en: Many Native Americans came to know the settlers not through happy thanksgivings
sentences.zh: 许多美洲原住民认识定居者并非通过快乐的感恩节

sentences.en: or even through war and colonization, but through slavery.
sentences.zh: 甚至也不是通过战争与殖民，而是通过奴隶制。

sentences.en: We say that there have been 12.5 million Africans forcibly transported across the Atlantic
sentences.zh: 我们常说，曾有1250万非洲人被强行运过大西洋，

sentences.en: as slaves into the New World.
sentences.zh: 作为奴隶来到新世界。

sentences.en: That is a very powerful thing to say,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有分量的说法，

sentences.en: and I wanted to get a rough sense of how Indian slavery compared to that.
sentences.zh: 而我想大致了解印第安人奴隶制与之相比如何。

sentences.en: So I came up with a figure of 2.5 to 5 million Native Americans
sentences.zh: 因此我得出这样一个数字：从哥伦布时代到1900年，

sentences.en: enslaved throughout the Americas since Columbus to 1900.
sentences.zh: 美洲各地共有250万到500万美洲原住民被奴役。

sentences.en: 2.5 to 5 million people.
This week on Hidden Brain, we explore this hidden history
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》中，我们将探讨这段被掩盖的历史，

sentences.en: and the psychological reasons it's remained submerged for so long.
sentences.zh: 以及它长期隐匿不为人知的心理原因。

sentences.en: Andres Resendez is a history professor at the University of California, Davis.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯·雷森德斯是加利福尼亚大学戴维斯分校的历史学教授。

sentences.en: He's the author of The Other Slavery,
sentences.zh: 他是《另一场奴隶制：

sentences.en: The Uncovered Story of Indian Enslavement in America.
sentences.zh: 美洲印第安人被奴役的不为人知的故事》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Andres, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: It is a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I want to begin by having you paint a picture for us.
sentences.zh: 我想先请你为我们描绘一幅画面。

sentences.en: And I want to start in 1495, when Christopher Columbus sends five ships back to Spain from the New World.
sentences.zh: 我想从1495年开始，当时克里斯托弗·哥伦布从新世界派出了五艘船返回西班牙。

sentences.en: On board are 550 captives, mostly from the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 船上载有550名俘虏，大部分来自加勒比地区。

sentences.en: Who are these people, and where is Columbus sending them?
sentences.zh: 这些人是谁？哥伦布要把他们送往哪里？

sentences.en: Well, Columbus has mounting problems because the riches that he thought he would find in the lands of Asia,
sentences.zh: 嗯，哥伦布面临的问题越来越多，因为他原以为能在亚洲的土地上找到的财富——

sentences.en: where he was hoping to go, were non-materializing.
sentences.zh: 也就是他希望去的地方——并没有出现。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, the costs of sending more fleets to the New World were mounting.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，向新世界派遣更多船队的成本却在不断攀升。

sentences.en: And so he decided that one good way to pay for these costs was by sending some Indians back to the slave markets of the Mediterranean,
sentences.zh: 因此他决定，支付这些成本的一个好方法就是把一些印第安人送回地中海的奴隶市场，

sentences.en: in this case, in particular, to Spain.
sentences.zh: 具体到这次，是送往西班牙。

sentences.en: And they selected, out of close to a thousand Native Americans, the best ones,
sentences.zh: 他们在近千名美洲原住民中挑选出最健壮的人，

sentences.en: crammed them into these ships and shipped them back to the Old World.
sentences.zh: 把他们塞进这些船里，运回了旧世界。

sentences.en: Besides the idea that the slave trade was part of a business model, there were also other elements of it.
sentences.zh: 除了将奴隶贸易视为商业模式的一部分外，其中还有其他因素。

sentences.en: You cite a letter that one of Columbus's childhood friends sends that reveals another aspect of how this famous explorer viewed the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 你引用了哥伦布的一位童年朋友写的一封信，这封信揭示了这位著名探险家看待奴隶贸易的另一个侧面。

sentences.en: What was in that letter?
sentences.zh: 那封信里写了什么？

sentences.en: Well, this is a letter by a childhood friend, Michele da Cuneo, an Italian, a fellow Genoese,
sentences.zh: 这是一个童年朋友写的信，名叫米歇尔·达·库内奥，是个意大利人，也是热那亚老乡，

sentences.en: who traveled with these indigenous slaves bound for Europe.
sentences.zh: 他与这批开往欧洲的本土奴隶同行。

sentences.en: And Columbus had actually given his friend a young Native American woman as a gift.
sentences.zh: 哥伦布实际上曾把一名年轻的美洲原住民女性作为礼物送给他的这位朋友。

sentences.en: And Cuneo is very explicit about the fact that in seeing her naked, he wanted to have sex with her.
sentences.zh: 库内奥非常明确地表示，在看到她赤身裸体时，他想要和她发生性关系。

sentences.en: It reveals the very terrible fact that the vast majority of these conquistadors were males.
sentences.zh: 这揭示了一个非常残酷的事实：绝大多数征服者都是男性。

sentences.en: And many of the indigenous victims ended up being both women and children.
sentences.zh: 许多原住民受害者最终都是妇女和儿童。

sentences.en: And so this is one instance of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是其中的一个例证。

sentences.en: You mentioned something in the book that I found surprising when I first read it,
sentences.zh: 你在书中提到了一个我初读时觉得惊讶的观点，

sentences.en: which is that women and children were often valued more highly as slaves than were men.
sentences.zh: 那就是妇女和儿童作为奴隶往往比成年男性更有价值。

sentences.en: Is sexual slavery part of what explains that?
sentences.zh: 性奴隶制是解释这一现象的原因之一吗？

sentences.en: It is surely one aspect of it.
sentences.zh: 这无疑是其中的一个方面。

sentences.en: The price differential that you are referring to was very surprising to me when I discovered that,
sentences.zh: 当我发现你所提到的这种价格差异时，我感到非常惊讶，

sentences.en: because in some instances, it could be that women were worth 50 or even 60 percent more than adult males.
sentences.zh: 因为在某些情况下，女性的身价可能比成年男性高出50%甚至60%。

sentences.en: So the scale was generally adult women were the highest valued slaves,
sentences.zh: 所以总体上的价格阶梯是：成年女性是价值最高的奴隶，

sentences.en: followed by girls, followed by boys, and followed by grown men.
sentences.zh: 其次是女孩，然后是男孩，最后是成年男子。

sentences.en: And there was a big drop off for the adult males.
sentences.zh: 成年男性的价格则大幅下降。

sentences.en: Maybe you can think about it as the antecedent of modern-day forms of sex trafficking.
sentences.zh: 或许你可以把这看作是现代形式人口贩运的前身。

sentences.en: That was certainly a part of it.
sentences.zh: 这确实是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Another part of it had to do with women's reproductive capabilities,
sentences.zh: 另一部分原因与女性的生育能力有关，

sentences.en: so they could produce yet more slaves.
sentences.zh: 这样她们就可以生出更多的奴隶。

sentences.en: So that was another factor.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一个因素。

sentences.en: Children were especially versatile because they could learn languages more easily than adults.
sentences.zh: 儿童尤其多才多艺，因为他们比成年人更容易学习语言。

sentences.en: They could, even in the fullness of time, identify with their captors.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们甚至会认同自己的俘获者。

sentences.en: So masters were especially keen on having children.
sentences.zh: 因此，主人特别热衷于拥有儿童。

sentences.en: Contrary to what we might think, slavery in America did not begin with Columbus or other European conquerors.
sentences.zh: 与我们可能认为的相反，美洲的奴隶制并不是始于哥伦布或其他欧洲征服者。

sentences.en: The roots of slavery run much deeper.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制的根源要深得多。

sentences.en: But the large-scale operations that Europeans put in place
sentences.zh: 但欧洲人建立的大规模行动

sentences.en: dramatically increased the scale and the scope of the practice.
sentences.zh: 极大地增加了这一做法的规模和范围。

sentences.en: We really don't know when slavery began in the New World,
sentences.zh: 我们其实并不知道新世界的奴隶制始于何时，

sentences.en: probably from the very beginning of the occupation of the continent.
sentences.zh: 大概从这片大陆开始有人占领之初就已经存在了。

sentences.en: What we do know is that there is plenty of archaeological and pictorial evidence,
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，有大量的考古和图像证据，

sentences.en: as well as some of the early chronicles of the New World,
sentences.zh: 以及一些关于新世界早期编年史的记录，

sentences.en: depict the enslavement of natives prior to the arrival of Europeans.
sentences.zh: 都描绘了欧洲人到达之前对原住民的奴役。

sentences.en: In the eastern seaboard of the United States, Iroquois peoples waged wars on neighboring groups
sentences.zh: 在美国东海岸，易洛魁人对邻近群体发动战争，

sentences.en: for the purpose of avenging their dead and replacing them with captives.
sentences.zh: 目的是为死者复仇并用俘虏取而代之。

sentences.en: In the Pacific Northwest, elite marriages were often sealed by providing slaves.
sentences.zh: 在太平洋西北地区，精英阶层的联姻通常通过提供奴隶来缔结。

sentences.en: So we know that these activities went on, and they were, however, very bound in specific cultural context.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道这些活动一直在进行，然而，它们高度局限于特定的文化背景中。

sentences.en: And so what changed with the arrival of the Europeans
sentences.zh: 因此，随着欧洲人的到来，改变之处在于

sentences.en: was that these culturally bound activities became commodified and expanded in scale
sentences.zh: 这些具有文化局限性的活动被商品化并扩大了规模，

sentences.en: until becoming something closer to what we would recognize as modern-day human trafficking.
sentences.zh: 直到变得更接近我们今天所识别的现代贩运人口。

sentences.en: You mentioned that by the 19th century, Brigham Young, one of the early leaders of the Mormon Church
sentences.zh: 你提到，到了19世纪，摩门教早期领袖之一、

sentences.en: and the founder of Salt Lake City, he has to decide whether Mormons can buy and sell slaves.
sentences.zh: 盐湖城创始人杨百翰，必须决定摩门教徒是否可以买卖奴隶。

sentences.en: What does he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: When the Mormons arrived in Utah, they found that the entire region had already been turned into
sentences.zh: 当摩门教徒抵达犹他州时，他们发现整个地区已经变成

sentences.en: slaving ground by natives themselves and by Hispanic merchants who were operating in the area.
sentences.zh: 原住民自己以及在该地区活动的西班牙裔商人猎捕奴隶的场所。

sentences.en: So from the very beginning, from the time they arrived, they found slavers offering them slaves,
sentences.zh: 因此从一开始，从他们到达的时候起，他们就发现奴隶贩子供给他们奴隶，

sentences.en: often children, who were tortured or kept outside in very cold conditions
sentences.zh: 通常是儿童，他们遭受折磨或被关在极冷的户外环境中，

sentences.en: as a tactic to force Mormons to acquire these Indians.
sentences.zh: 以此作为强迫摩门教徒收留这些印第安人的战术。

sentences.en: And by 1850 or 1851, Young and other leaders, Mormon leaders,
sentences.zh: 到1850年或1851年，杨和其他领袖，即摩门教领袖，

sentences.en: decide that the best way to deal with this situation is to actually,
sentences.zh: 决定处理这种情况的最佳方法实际上是，

sentences.en: their term was to buy these Indians into freedom.
sentences.zh: 用他们的术语来说，是把这些印第安人买向自由。

sentences.en: Eventually, groups like the Mormons found ways to rationalize their beliefs in slavery
sentences.zh: 最终，像摩门教徒这样的群体找到了将他们对奴隶制的信仰合理化的方法，

sentences.en: and to reconcile it in some ways with the mission of the church.
sentences.zh: 并在某种程度上将其与教会的使命调和起来。

sentences.en: And of course, this has parallels with other ideas and ideologies that you describe in the book.
sentences.zh: 当然，这与你在书中描述的其他观点和意识形态有相似之处。

sentences.en: European settlers and colonists apparently had long linked character with latitude,
sentences.zh: 欧洲定居者和殖民者显然长期将性格与纬度联系在一起，

sentences.en: and they used this as a justification for slavery.
sentences.zh: 他们以此作为奴隶制的正当理由。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So these are very ancient beliefs about the character of people,
sentences.zh: 因此，这些是非常古老的关于人们性格的信念，

sentences.en: depending on where they lived on earth.
sentences.zh: 取决于他们居住在地球上的哪个地方。

sentences.en: So they believe, for example, that the people who lived in the cold regions of earth
sentences.zh: 例如，他们认为住在地球寒冷地区的居民

sentences.en: were very bold and intrepid, but they lacked intelligence.
sentences.zh: 非常勇敢无畏，但缺乏智慧。

sentences.en: And conversely, that the people close to the equator were intelligent
sentences.zh: 相反，靠近赤道的人很有智慧

sentences.en: and therefore would make great slaves, but lacked in courage and boldness.
sentences.zh: 因此是非常好的奴隶人选，但缺乏勇气和无畏精神。

sentences.en: And of course, the perfect balance of these two traits existed in the temperate areas,
sentences.zh: 当然，这两种特质的完美平衡存在于温带地区，

sentences.en: and by that you have to read the European Mediterranean region where Spain, England, France, etc.
sentences.zh: 说到这，你必须联想到西班牙、英国、法国等国存在的欧洲地中海地区，

sentences.en: existed
sentences.zh: 存在于那里

sentences.en: and had a perfect blend of these characteristics.
sentences.zh: 并拥有这些特征的完美融合。

sentences.en: And so that was one way to rationalize the enslavement of natives
sentences.zh: 所以这是将奴隶化原住民的行为合理化的一种方式，

sentences.en: and other peoples in sub-Saharan Africa, for that matter.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，也包括撒哈拉以南非洲的其他民族。

sentences.en: Andres has many examples that challenge how we think about slavery in America.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯举了许多例子，挑战了我们对美洲奴隶制的固有看法。

sentences.en: We might think of the West Coast as largely being uninvolved in slavery.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会认为西海岸在很大程度上与奴隶制无关。

sentences.en: In reality, the gold rush ignited a need for labor,
sentences.zh: 现实中，淘金热点燃了对劳动力的需求，

sentences.en: and enslaved Native Americans were brought in to meet it.
sentences.zh: 被奴役的美洲原住民被带到那里以满足这一需求。

sentences.en: Two brothers who set up a cattle and mining operation north of what is today San Francisco
sentences.zh: 有两兄弟在如今旧金山以北建立了一个养牛和采矿场，

sentences.en: were especially sadistic owners.
sentences.zh: 他们是极其残虐的主人。

sentences.en: Sometimes they used slaves for target practice.
sentences.zh: 有时他们把奴隶当作靶子来练习射击。

sentences.en: During the Civil War, Union soldiers stationed in New Mexico
sentences.zh: 南北战争期间，驻扎在新墨西哥州的联邦士兵

sentences.en: used systematic violence to address what the federal government saw as a law and order issue,
sentences.zh: 使用系统性暴力来解决联邦政府视为法律与秩序问题的事端，

sentences.en: the so-called Indian problem.
sentences.zh: 即所谓的“印第安人问题”。

sentences.en: The method to solve this problem was to essentially relocate the entire Navajo Nation
sentences.zh: 解决这个问题的办法基本上是将整个纳瓦霍族

sentences.en: from western New Mexico to eastern New Mexico in what was known as the Long Walk.
sentences.zh: 从新墨西哥州西部迁移到新墨西哥州东部，这就是著名的“长途步行”。

sentences.en: And this process essentially put a very large population in a very vulnerable situation.
sentences.zh: 这一过程基本上将庞大的人口置于极其脆弱的境地。

sentences.en: Andres describes the work of an investigative journalist, John Kenneth Turner.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯描述了一位调查记者约翰·肯尼斯·特纳的工作。

sentences.en: He uncovered many of the ways that plantation owners worked around the ban on slavery
sentences.zh: 他揭露了庄园主在20世纪很长一段时间里规避奴隶禁令的许多手段。

sentences.en: well into the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 他伪装成美国投资者前往尤卡坦半岛。

sentences.en: And he went to the Yucatan Peninsula posing as an American investor.
sentences.zh: 于是特纳得以接触到这些种植园，并进行实地观察。

sentences.en: And so Turner had access to these plantations, was able to look at this.
sentences.zh: 当时奴隶制在墨西哥是完全被禁的。

sentences.en: Slavery was completely forbidden in Mexico at that time.
sentences.zh: 但他赢得了这些庄园主的信任，他们说，

sentences.en: But he was able to gain the confidence of these owners who said,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我们知道印第安奴隶制是违法的，

sentences.en: well, you know, we know that Indian slavery is prohibited,
sentences.zh: 但我们有一种绕过这个问题的方法，

sentences.en: but we have a way to get around this problem,
sentences.zh: 那就是这些印第安人欠了我们的债。

sentences.en: which is that these Indians are indebted to us.
sentences.zh: 只要有债务存在，他们就无法离开这些场所，也就是种植园。

sentences.en: And as long as there's a debt, they are unable to leave the premises, the plantations.
sentences.zh: 你可以在市场上买下他们。

sentences.en: And you could buy them in the market.
sentences.zh: 种植园主将此合理化的方式是，你买下的其实不是这个人，

sentences.en: And the way the planters rationalized this is that you are not really buying the person,
sentences.zh: 而是买下了这笔债务。

sentences.en: but you are buying the debt.
sentences.zh: 而人是随着债务一起归你的。

sentences.en: And the person goes with the debt.
sentences.zh: 许多人在许多世代里促成了对原住民的大规模奴役。

sentences.en: Many people over many generations helped enable the vast scale of enslavement of indigenous people.
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们的教科书和公众意识中只有关于这段历史的零星记录呢？

sentences.en: So why are they only scattered records of this history in our textbooks and public consciousness?
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯，你把你的书命名为《另一场奴隶制》。

sentences.en: Andres, you call your book The Other Slavery.
sentences.zh: 为什么你把原住民被奴役的历史

sentences.en: Why do you describe the history of the enslavement of native peoples
sentences.zh: 与美国非洲奴隶的经历进行对比来描述？

sentences.en: in contrast with the experience of African slaves in the United States?
sentences.zh: 因为与几个世纪以来一直合法

sentences.en: Because unlike African slavery, which was legal for centuries
sentences.zh: 并得到世界各地国家和帝国支持的非洲奴隶制不同，

sentences.en: and sanctioned by states and empires around the world,
sentences.zh: 印第安人奴隶制很早就被宣布为非法。

sentences.en: Indian slavery was very early on made illegal.
sentences.zh: 甚至在哥伦布首次踏上新世界八年之后也是如此。

sentences.en: Even eight years after Columbus first set foot in the New World,
sentences.zh: 即使在哥伦布首次踏上新世界八年之后也是如此

sentences.en: there were questions about the legality of the enslavement of Indians.
sentences.zh: 当时曾有人对奴役印第安人的合法性提出过质疑。

sentences.en: And as early as 1542, the Spanish crown outlawed Indian slavery under all circumstances.
sentences.zh: 早在1542年，西班牙王室就在所有情况下宣布印第安人奴隶制为非法。

sentences.en: However, because Native American labor had been essential to all of the economic activities going on
sentences.zh: 然而，由于美洲原住民的劳动力对当时所有的经济活动都至关重要，

sentences.en: during these first generation of colonialism,
sentences.zh: 在殖民统治的第一代人期间，

sentences.en: it was unthinkable for the European colonists to do without native slaves.
sentences.zh: 欧洲殖民者根本无法想象没有原住民奴隶的日子。

sentences.en: And so they very quickly devised all kinds of subterfuges and euphemisms
sentences.zh: 因此，他们很快想出了各种借口和委婉说法，

sentences.en: in order to continue to profit from the coerced labor of natives by calling it different names.
sentences.zh: 通过换用不同的称呼，来继续从原住民被强迫的劳动中牟利。

sentences.en: So I call it other slavery in the sense that not only that it target Native Americans as opposed to Africans,
sentences.zh: 所以我称之为“另一种奴役”，不仅是因为它的目标是美洲原住民而非非洲人，

sentences.en: but also in the sense that it encompassed a multiplicity of institutions or labor practices
sentences.zh: 还因为它包含了一系列多种多样的制度或劳动实践，

sentences.en: that we really need to put together and understand together
sentences.zh: 如果我们想要了解我所说的这种“另一种奴役”的规模，

sentences.en: if we want to gain a sense of the scope of these other slavery, as I call it.
sentences.zh: 我们就必须把这些东西结合在一起去认识和理解。

sentences.en: So I think the point that you're trying to make is that slavery in some ways is an adaptable concept.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你想要表达的观点是，在某些方面，奴隶制是一个具有适应性的概念。

sentences.en: So in some cases, people, of course, are chained and tortured,
sentences.zh: 因此，在某些情况下，人们当然会被戴上锁链并遭受折磨，

sentences.en: but in other cases, coercion can take on different forMs.
sentences.zh: 但在其他情况下，强迫劳动可以采取不同的形式。

sentences.en: At the same time, it's obviously important to distinguish between somebody who's enslaved
sentences.zh: 与此同时，显然也很重要的一点是，要区分被奴役的人

sentences.en: and somebody who's working in, for example, just difficult labor conditions.
sentences.zh: 和仅仅处于艰难劳动条件下的工作者。

sentences.en: In the way that you have gone about your study, how are you defining who constitutes a slave?
sentences.zh: 在你进行研究的过程中，你是如何定义谁才构成奴隶的？

sentences.en: This definitional problem came from the very beginning of the project.
sentences.zh: 这个关于定义的问题在项目一开始就出现了。

sentences.en: So I came up with a list of four characteristics that made these other slavery fit the bill of what I call slavery.
sentences.zh: 因此我总结出了四个特征，让这些“另一种奴役”符合我所谓的奴隶制的标准。

sentences.en: And so one of them was that natives usually were forcibly moved far away from their place of origin.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是，原住民通常会被强行带到远离其原籍地的地方。

sentences.en: And this may not have occurred at the very beginning,
sentences.zh: 这种情况在一开始可能并没有发生，

sentences.en: but very quickly the owners came to realize that enslaving natives who lived very close to them
sentences.zh: 但很快奴隶主们便意识到，奴役那些住在他们附近的本地原住民

sentences.en: could open themselves to retaliation.
sentences.zh: 可能会给自己招致报复。

sentences.en: And so the way to do it was to send them to faraway places.
sentences.zh: 因此解决办法就是把他们送到遥远的地方去。

sentences.en: So displacement to faraway places was one of the characteristics that I early on realized
sentences.zh: 所以流放到远方是我很早就意识到的特征之一，

sentences.en: was common to many of these labor practices.
sentences.zh: 这也是许多此类劳动实践的共同点。

sentences.en: Second of all, they were unable to leave their place of work.
sentences.zh: 其次，他们无法离开工作场所。

sentences.en: Whether you were talking about indebted workers or people serving out their sentences
sentences.zh: 无论你讨论的是负债劳工、服刑人员

sentences.en: or people entrusted, etc., they could not willingly leave their place of work.
sentences.zh: 还是受托监管的人等等，他们都无法自主离开工作场所。

sentences.en: Third characteristic was the use of violence or at least the threat of use of violence in order to seek compliance.
sentences.zh: 第三个特征是使用暴力，或者至少是以使用暴力相威胁，以迫使他们顺从。

sentences.en: And finally, there was the question of payment, which was often non-existent.
sentences.zh: 最后是报酬问题，这通常是不存在的。

sentences.en: Or if it existed, it was so low that it was practically symbolic.
sentences.zh: 或者即使有报酬，也是少得可怜，几乎只具象征意义。

sentences.en: One of the ideas in Andres' book has less to do with history and more to do with psychology.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯书中的一个观点与其说是历史，不如说是心理学。

sentences.en: It has to do with how our minds tend to categorize historical events.
sentences.zh: 它关系到我们的头脑倾向于如何对历史事件进行分类。

sentences.en: When I talk about enslaved people in America, you might think of people brought over from Africa.
sentences.zh: 当我谈到美洲的被奴役者时，你可能会想到从非洲运来的人。

sentences.en: But if I talk about Native Americans, you're more likely to think of dispossession and exclusion.
sentences.zh: 但如果我谈到美洲原住民，你更有可能会想到被剥夺土地和被排挤。

sentences.en: We are so focused on these categories that have been drilled into us from childhood
sentences.zh: 我们太专注于这些从小就被灌输给我们的分类了，

sentences.en: that we seem unable to escape our historical myopia, as I call it in the book.
sentences.zh: 以至于我们似乎无法摆脱我书中所称的历史近视。

sentences.en: And this is especially difficult to break in the case of Native Americans
sentences.zh: 在美洲原住民的情况下，这种观念尤其难以打破，

sentences.en: because, as I have explained, this was not a legal institution
sentences.zh: 因为正如我所解释的，这不是一项法律制度，

sentences.en: and it was not a single institution, but it was a multiplicity of labor practices.
sentences.zh: 它也不是单一的制度，而是一系列多种多样的劳动实践。

sentences.en: And so that has conspired to prevent us from realizing both the scale
sentences.zh: 因此，这导致我们既无法意识到这些“另一种奴役”的规模，

sentences.en: and even the very existence of these other slavery.
sentences.zh: 甚至也无法意识到它们真实存在过。

sentences.en: One of the things that put your work into context for me is that you pointed out
sentences.zh: 让我的工作得以放在特定语境中的原因之一，是你指出

sentences.en: that West Africa saw a population decline of about 20% as a result of slavery.
sentences.zh: 西非由于奴役人口减少了大约20%。

sentences.en: And, of course, the scale of that is just incomprehensible.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种规模简直是不可思议的。

sentences.en: Indigenous people in the New World also suffered catastrophic declines in population
sentences.zh: 新世界的原住民也因奴隶制而遭受了灾难性的人口骤减。

sentences.en: as a result of slavery.
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Could you talk about that for a second?
sentences.zh: 我不想把这变成一场谁更悲惨的竞赛。

sentences.en: I don't want to make this into a race to the bottom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，非洲人和美洲原住民都在

sentences.en: I mean, both Africans and Native Americans lost immeasurably
sentences.zh: 瘟疫流行与奴役的双重交织下遭受了无可估量的损失。

sentences.en: as a result of these nexus of epidemics and enslavement.
sentences.zh: 我可以谈谈这种联系。

sentences.en: And I can talk about that relationship.
sentences.zh: 但我想要强调的观点是，就美洲原住民而言，

sentences.en: But the point that I make is that in the case of Native Americans,
sentences.zh: 特别是在加勒比海和墨西哥湾的一些地区，

sentences.en: especially in the Caribbean and some regions in the Gulf of Mexico,
sentences.zh: 人口消亡的程度是惊人的。

sentences.en: the level of decimation was staggering.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它远大于20%。

sentences.en: I mean, it was much greater than 20%.
It could be 80%, 90%.
sentences.zh: 因此，记住这些惊人的数字是很有必要的。

sentences.en: So it is good to bear in mind the staggering numbers.
sentences.zh: 被奴役与瘟疫和传染病的传播之间有什么关系？

sentences.en: What is the relationship between enslavement and the spread of epidemics and infection?
sentences.zh: 这是一种协同关系。

sentences.en: It's one of synergy.
sentences.zh: 但在加勒比海地区，我发现的情况是，流行病

sentences.en: But what I found in the case of the Caribbean is that epidemic disease
sentences.zh: 本质上减少了奴隶的数量，

sentences.en: essentially reduced the number of slaves,
sentences.zh: 这促使奴隶贩子对其他岛屿发动袭击。

sentences.en: which prompted slavers to launch raids into other islands.
sentences.zh: 而这些袭击反过来又传播了流行病。

sentences.en: And the launching of these raids, in turn, spread epidemic disease.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个完整的恶性循环，在加勒比地区造成了巨大的毁灭。

sentences.en: So it was a complete reinforcing circle that resulted in great devastation in the case of the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 美国的感恩节就要到了。

sentences.en: We have Thanksgiving coming up in the United States.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一个我们向彼此表达感激和谢意的节日。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's an occasion where we express gratitude and thanks to one another.
sentences.zh: 但它也是一个进行历史反思的时刻。

sentences.en: But it's also a moment of historical reflection.
sentences.zh: 我们在某种程度上感谢那些帮助早期定居者度过极其艰难冬天的原住民。

sentences.en: And we give thanks in some ways for Native peoples who helped the early settlers through a very difficult winter.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，当你坐在感恩节的餐桌旁，带着你所拥有的历史知识，

sentences.en: I'm wondering, as you sit down at Thanksgiving, knowing the history that you do,
sentences.zh: 你是如何看待感恩节的？

sentences.en: how do you see Thanksgiving?
sentences.zh: 你对它的看法发生改变了吗？

sentences.en: Have you come to think of it differently?
sentences.zh: 嗯，通过这本书，我对美洲整个早期殖民时期的看法都发生了改变。

sentences.en: Well, I have come to think of the whole early colonial period of the Americas differently as a result of this book.
sentences.zh: 我对在这个严酷环境中生存的艰难有了全新的认识，

sentences.en: I have gained a newfound appreciation for the difficulty of surviving in this tough environment,
sentences.zh: 也意识到了所有人类群体在追求这些目标时的冷酷无情，

sentences.en: the ruthlessness with which all human groups pursued these goals
sentences.zh: 为了达到目的，他们甘愿利用其他人类。

sentences.en: and were willing to avail themselves to other humans in order to achieve their goals.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这不是一部好人与坏人的历史。

sentences.en: As I said, this is not a history of good people and bad people.
sentences.zh: 我的确发现了一些没有抓捕俘虏或奴隶的原住民群体。

sentences.en: I did find some indigenous groups who did not take captives or slaves.
sentences.zh: 往往是因为他们的规模太小，或者由于环境原因，

sentences.en: Oftentimes, because they were too small or because of environmental reasons,
sentences.zh: 获取更多的人根本没有意义，因为那也意味着要多养几张嘴。

sentences.en: it made no sense to acquire more people because they would also mean more mouths to feed.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我发现所有有能力做到这一点并从中获利的人都这么做了。

sentences.en: But other than that, I found that everybody who was in a position to do it and profit from it did it.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是一本很难写书，因为在书的最后一部分，

sentences.en: And in some ways, it's a difficult book to write because in the final part of the book,
sentences.zh: 我提到这些形式的奴役与我们现在所称的现代奴役形式并没有太大区别，

sentences.en: I mentioned that these forms of enslavement were not very dissimilar to the forms that we now call modern forms of enslavement
sentences.zh: 因为尽管奴隶制如今在全世界已被禁止，

sentences.en: in the sense that slavery is today prohibited all over the world,
sentences.zh: 但根据“自由行走基金会”的最新估计，仍有4500多万人

sentences.en: yet some over 45 million people, according to the latest estimates of the Walk Free Foundation,
sentences.zh: 处于现代奴役状态中。

sentences.en: are in a condition of modern-day enslavement.
sentences.zh: 这些人被奴役的方式在某些方面让人联想到

sentences.en: And the ways in which these people are enslaved are in some ways reminiscent
sentences.zh: 美洲原住民在长达400年的时间里所经历的一切。

sentences.en: of what Native Americans experienced for a period of 400 years.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯·雷森德斯是加利福尼亚大学戴维斯分校的历史学教授。

sentences.en: Andres Resendez is a history professor at the University of California, Davis.
sentences.zh: 他是《另一种奴役：美洲印第安人奴役的不为人知的故事》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He's the author of The Other Slavery, The Uncovered Story of Indian Enslavement in America.
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯，谢谢你今天来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.

sentences.zh: 我们本周的无名英雄是马萨诸塞州斯旺西的杰克·麦卡锡。

sentences.en: Our unsung hero this week is Jack McCarthy of Swansea, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 他在上周去世了，但他曾是一名高中历史老师、

sentences.en: He passed away last week, but he was a high school history teacher,
sentences.zh: 足球和棒球教练，并在斯旺西担任了近二十年的学区总监。

sentences.en: a football and baseball coach, and superintendent of schools in Swansea for nearly two decades.
sentences.zh: 1985年，他允许一名患有艾滋病的儿童去公立学校上学，从而上了全国头条新闻，

sentences.en: In 1985, he made national headlines by allowing a child with AIDS to attend public school
sentences.zh: 当时全国各地的学校系统都在将这样的儿童拒之门外。

sentences.en: at a time when school systems across the country were turning such children away.
sentences.zh: 在他的讣告中，人们提到他具有坚韧、信念、毅力、勇气和爱尔兰式的固执。

sentences.en: In his obituary, people noted that he had strength, conviction, fortitude, courage, and Irish stubbornness.
sentences.zh: 我们认识杰克是因为他是我们同事玛吉·彭曼的祖父，

sentences.en: We know Jack because he was the grandfather of our own Maggie Penman,
sentences.zh: 我可以作证，他赋予了玛吉所有这些优秀的品质。

sentences.en: and I can attest he gave Maggie all those qualities.
